related_questions.question: What is the fastest way to treat COVID symptoms?
related_questions.snippet: Manage Symptoms Most people with COVID-19 have mild illness and can recover at home. You can treat symptoms with over-the-counter medicines, such as acetaminophen or ibuprofen, to help feel better.
related_questions.title: Types of COVID-19 Treatment - CDC

related_questions.question: How long are you contagious with COVID?
related_questions.snippet: People with COVID-19 can be infectious from 1–2 days before and up to 8–10 days after symptoms begin. The majority of transmission appears to occur during the early periods of infection, particularly in the 1–2 days before symptoms start and within the first few days of symptom onset.
related_questions.title: COVID-19 | Yellow Book - CDC

related_questions.question: How to get COVID out of your system?

text_blocks.snippet: To get COVID-19 out of your system, focus on rest, hydration, and managing symptoms. While there's no specific cure to remove the virus, your body's immune system will naturally work to fight it off. Symptom management can include over-the-counter medications for fever and pain, and ensuring adequate fluid intake.
snippet_highlighted_words: focus on rest, hydration, and managing symptoms

list.title: Rest:
list.snippet: Allow your body to focus on healing by getting plenty of sleep and avoiding strenuous activities.

list.title: Isolation:
list.snippet: To prevent spreading the virus, isolate yourself from others, especially those at higher risk of severe illness.

list.title: Fever and Pain:
list.snippet: Use over-the-counter medications like acetaminophen (Tylenol) or ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin) to manage fever and aches.

list.title: Cough and Congestion:
list.snippet: Consider using a cool mist humidifier or taking a warm, steamy shower to help loosen congestion and ease breathing, says UnityPoint Health.

list.title: Hydration:
list.snippet: Drink plenty of fluids to stay hydrated, as dehydration can worsen symptoms.

list.title: When to Seek Medical Advice:
list.snippet: If you experience severe symptoms like persistent fever, difficulty breathing, chest pain, or confusion, seek immediate medical attention.

list.title: Treatment Options:
list.snippet: A doctor can assess your condition and may recommend specific treatments or medications depending on the severity of your illness.

list.title: Lukewarm Baths:
list.snippet: A lukewarm bath can help regulate body temperature and boost circulation, especially if you have a fever.

list.title: Steam Inhalation:
list.snippet: Inhaling steam from a bowl of hot water or a warm shower can help loosen congestion according to UnityPoint Health.

list.title: Avoid Overbundling:
list.snippet: If you have a fever, avoid overdressing or bundling up, as this can trap heat.

list.title: Recovery Time:
list.snippet: Mild to moderate COVID-19 cases typically resolve within one to two weeks, says UnityPoint Health.

list.title: Listen to Your Body:
list.snippet: Pay attention to your body's signals and allow for a gradual return to normal activities as you recover.
